taxonomy:
Below is a mechanic‑based taxonomy for grid logic games. Each category lists the games from your set that primarily fit that mechanic. (Many puzzles mix mechanics; this groups them by the dominant action/goal.)

1) Edge-based single-loop drawing (draw one closed loop on grid edges; clues steer where the loop goes)
- Slitherlink
- Masyu
- Moon-or-Sun
- Yajilin
- Suraromu
- Dotchi-Loop
- Mid-loop

2) Cell-based paths/snakes and pair connections (draw paths through cells; usually open paths, snakes, or connections between marked points)
- Numberlink
- Hebi
- Nurimeizu
- Nurimisaki
- Chained Block
- Nagareru

3) Graph connection on island nodes (bridge-building on a point network)
- Hashiwokakero

4) Region partition/tiling (cover all cells by partitioning into regions with given size/shape rules)
- Rectangular partitions:
  - Shikaku
  - Double Choco
  - Choco Banana
- Polyomino-size partitions:
  - Fillomino
  - Evolomino
  - Five Cells
- Shaped/L-shaped partitions:
  - Sashigane
- Sum/recipe-driven partitions:
  - Yosenabe
- Move/assign numbers within rooms (room Latin-style placement):
  - Satogaeri

5) Black–white shading/painting with connectivity, visibility, or local counts (decide which cells are shaded; white/black areas must meet global/local rules)
- Island/wall family:
  - Nurikabe
  - Nuritwin
  - Tilepaint
- Roomed shading/run-length rules:
  - Heyawake
- Visibility/line-of-sight:
  - Kurodoko (Kuromasu)
  - Akari (Light Up)
- Local sum/count around symbols:
  - Kurotto
- Liar/consistency variants:
  - Usowan
- Row/column deduplication via shading:
  - Hitori
- Per-room piece-shaped shading:
  - LITS (tetromino per room, with global adjacency bans)
  - Norinori (domino per room)
- Geometric piece placement that constrains white rectangles:
  - Shakashaka
- Stone/mark placement as shading variant:
  - Sto-stone

6) Number placement with row/column constraints (Latin/spacing/inequality or arithmetic filling; no shading/loop as the main task)
- Sudoku
- Ripple Effect (Suguru)
- Makaro
- Nansuke
- Juosan

7) Line/edge drawing networks without a single-loop requirement (build lines with degree/length constraints; can form trees or sets of segments)
- Pencils

Notes
- Some titles span multiple families (e.g., Yajilin mixes loop-drawing with shaded cells; LITS/Norinori are shading but piece-constrained by rooms). Here they’re placed where solvers usually “think first.”
